subject: Post-demo: hyperscaler delta & unit-econ verification — next tests
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@optiscale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: hyperscaler delta & unit-econ verification — next tests

Hi Sarah — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed verification plan so we keep momentum: 

Recap (what we saw on the call)
- Hyperscaler A showed lower cost in their native benchmark for long-sequence text (8k tokens) but we saw a 20–30% latency tail and no KV cache persistence option.
- OptiScale’s primary use is multi-turn assistant with ~40% prefix re-use (chat-like). That means cache hit rates matter more than peak per-token raw throughput.
- Our hosted Redwood inference demo used model: redwood-v1-gguf (quantized variant), batching=8 with warm KV cache; the per-1M token extrapolated unit cost we presented assumed 65% cache hit.

Open asks from your side
- Confirm target SLA for 95th percentile latency and acceptable cold-cache latency.
- Confirm expected concurrency profile (average and spike).

Proposed verification tests (what we can run next) — goal: apples-to-apples economics vs hyperscaler claims
1) Unit-econ run (1M tokens): batch_size=8, warm KV cache (simulate 65% hit). Measure tokens/sec, 95p latency, and per-token cost. (Target: 48–72 hours run to smooth noise).
2) Latency bucket: batch_size=1, cold cache (simulate first-turn queries). Measure 95p and 99p latencies and cost impact per 1k requests.
3) Mixed workload: 60/40 mix (chat vs single-shot), concurrency 120, run for 6 hours to capture autoscale behavior and tail effects.

Attachments: unit_econ_sheet.xlsx (baseline numbers + assumptions), demo-recording.mp4 (45m demo).

Next steps / asks
- If this plan looks good I’ll loop in infra to schedule the runs and share a short mutual action plan.
- Could you confirm the opt-in test dataset (PII-scrubbed) and any isolation constraints for the runs?

I’m copying Ben and Priyom to pick up the scheduling and run ownership.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.com]
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@optiscale.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Cho <mike.cho@optiscale.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hyperscaler delta & unit-econ verification — next tests

Thanks Jordan — very clear, appreciate the write-up. A couple clarifications before we lock the test plan: 

- For the unit-econ run, can you break out the model size & quantization assumptions (fp16 vs int8 vs gguf)? Hyperscaler A appears to be using fp16 + proprietary kernel that improves long-sequence throughput; want to ensure we compare equivalent model variants.
- What tokenization model did you use for the 1M projection? We have two payload families (customer messages vs system context) with different avg token lengths.
- On concurrency: our baseline is ~50 sustained QPS with 6x daily spikes; for pilot we can open to 150 for short windows.

Two asks from me:
1) Please share a one-page mutual action plan (timeline, responsibilities) so procurement can track.
2) Can you confirm whether Redwood can produce an audit trace (per-request latency + cost attribution) for the 6-hour mixed run — we need that for our SRE review.

If you can send the assumptions & MAP today we’ll get procurement and SRE eyes on it Monday.

— Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Platform Engineering, OptiScale
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@optiscale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hyperscaler delta & unit-econ verification — next tests

Sarah — thanks, noted. Short answers inline and attached a one-page assumptions doc. See attachments: assumptions_breakdown.md (quick bullets).

- Model/quantization: demo used redwood-v1-gguf (int8-like gguf quant profile). We can also run redwood-v1-fp16 for a direct fp16 comparison; expect ~10–15% higher throughput for fp16 on the same hardware but also ~20–25% higher raw cost per GPU-hour.
- Tokenization: we used the unified tokenizer v1 with avg tokens per message = 14 for customer messages, 70 for system prompts. In the unit_econ_sheet.xlsx you can flip the avg token assumption.
- Audit trace: yes — Redwood can export per-request traces (timestamp, route, model_version, latency_ms, token_count, cost_units). We’ll provide a sample CSV after the mixed run; full export available via the private S3 link in the MAP.

Attached is the one-page Mutual Action Plan (inline summary below):
- Week 1 (Mon–Wed): finalize test dataset + sign-off on isolation (OptiScale).
- Week 1 (Thu–Fri): unit-econ run (1M tokens) + produce summary report.
- Week 2 (Mon): latency bucket run (batch=1 cold cache) + audit traces.
- Week 2 (Tue): mixed workload run (6 hours) + deliverables: per-request CSV, cost breakdown, dashboard screenshots.
- Owners: Redwood (Jordan, Ben) — run orchestration + traces; OptiScale (Sarah, Mike) — dataset + procurement sign-off.

If that timeline works, Ben and Priyom will pick the exact run windows and share access details.

— Jordan
